newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Prices steady to lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Prices steady to lower.

text.p: Millfeed prices were steady to lower on Thursday as dealers shrugged off a Food and Drug Administration plan to ban ruminant tissue use in animal feed.
The FDA on Thursday proposed to prohibit using tissues from ruminants -- animals such as cows, sheep and goats -- in the production of feedstuffs.
Dealers said millfeeds do not compete directly with the higher protein meat and bone meal and if the ban went through, a substitute like soybean meal would be used.
"It would make a difference in possibly soybean meal and canola meal, things of that nature," a Buffalo dealer said.
It would not affect the millfeed market," a Tennessee dealer said. "The proposed ban would help the soymeal market because soybean meal is a high protein concentrate."

Soybean meal typically has a 44 to 48 percent protein content. "Meat and bone meal are a high protein feed ingredient which has 50 percent protein while millfeeds are about 15 to 16 percent," he said.
"Obviously it would hurt the price of meat and bonemeal because there will be less homes for it," the dealer said.
Dealers said the proposal would also help feather meal, poultry meal and to some degree, cottonseed meal.
Feeders have already voluntarily scaled back on meat scrap in dairy feeds, a Carolinas dealer said. "They did that about a year ago," he said.

The proposal was made in an effort to protect U.S. livestock from transmissable degenerative neurological diseases and specifically, so-called mad cow disease, or bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE).
